title: Analysing LLM Persona Generation and Fairness Interpretation in Polarised Geopolitical Contexts

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to generate Palestinian and Israeli personas using fill-in-the-blank templates under various experimental conditions (e.g., war vs. non-war contexts, different assigned roles) and comparing the distributional disparities in assigned attributes.
Analyzing the distribution of socioeconomic status (lower-class, middle-class, upper-class) assigned to generated personas based on their geopolitical identity and the presence of a conflict context.
Evaluating the types of jobs models assign to different identities, specifically contrasting the assignment of high-status professional roles versus survival-oriented or manual labor jobs.

Measuring the proportions of inferred genders (male, female, non-binary) in generated personas and analyzing how these distributions skew based on nationality, conflict contexts, and the introduction of debiasing prompts.

Comparing the inferred attributes, such as socioeconomic status, occupation, and emotional appearance descriptors, assigned to 'child' versus 'adult' personas across the different geopolitical groups.
